title: Papal consecration of wax Agnus Dei images begs God to give them power against devil, storm, plague, and epilepsy
source_text: XXVIII. Idem dico de cereis illis imagunculis, quae agnus Dei vulgo nominantur, & quas Papa consecrare solet anno primo sui Pontificatus, & etiam post, septimo quoque anno, ut sint symbolicae quaedam imagines Domini nostri Jesu Christi, qui est verus Dei Agnus qui tollit peccata mundi. Nam Papa, dum illas consecrat, multis iteratis precibus Deum rogat, ut imagines illae virtutem accipiant contra diabolicas versutias, contra tempestates, contra pestem, contra morbum caducum, aliaque mala atque incommoda. Ut videre est in libro sacrarum ceremoniarum capite cui titulus est de consecratione Agnus Dei. Ubi inter plures alias orationes similes, una est in qua Papa quaedam praefatus sic Deum alloquitur, sicut ille Agnus de cujus sanguine postes & superlimina domus liniebantur, immolatus, populum tuum a persecutione Aegyptiaca, media nocte liberavit: & quemadmodum ille Agnus innocens tua voluntate immolatus in ara crucis Jesus Christus filius, Protoplastum nostrum de diabolica potestate eripuit, sic isti agni immaculati virtutem accipiant, quos consecrandos offerimus in conspectu Divinae Majestatis tuae. Tu eos benedicere, sanctificare, & consecrare digneris, ut tua larga benedictione sanctificati eandem virtutem accipiant contra omnes Diabolicas versutias, & fraudes maligni spiritus.
pass_a_gloss: I say the same of those little wax images which are commonly called agnus Dei, and which the Pope is accustomed to consecrate in the first year of his Pontificate, and also afterward, every seventh year as well, that they may be certain symbolic images of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is the true Lamb of God who takes away the sins of the world (John 1:29). For the Pope, while he consecrates them, asks God with many repeated prayers that those images may receive virtue against diabolical wiles, against storms, against plague, against the falling sickness, and other evils and inconveniences. As may be seen in the book of sacred ceremonies in the chapter titled on the consecration of the Agnus Dei… that, sanctified by Your large blessing, they may receive the same virtue against all Diabolical wiles and the frauds of the evil spirit.
pass_b_english: Wax Agnus Dei tokens—symbolic ‘Lamb’ images—are consecrated with papal prayers that they receive power against demons, storms, plague, and epilepsy (cf. John 1:29).

choices.english: on the consecration of the Agnus Dei
